headline: Will I find a new soulmate after loss?
note: generated from REVIEW-new-voice.md — not a wired draft

a: You turned the Magician. Three backs, and no way to know — yours was the one who came ready.
Look at his table. A cup, a coin, a blade and a wand, all of them out.
You asked whether you'll find a new soulmate after your loss. What catches me is how much is laid out on that table.
Still, nobody has come. And you're the one left holding the question.
Whatever is in the way of this holds steady, and it hasn't shifted. I don't think this began with you.
Let me look closer at what's holding it…
b: You turned the Hanged Man. Nothing showed which was which, and yours was the card still growing.
Look at the wood he hangs from. It's alive, with green leaves on it.
You asked whether you'll find a new soulmate after your loss. What holds my eye is living wood with a rope through it.
And yet nobody has come. And you're the one asking whether there's another.
Something stands between you and this, close by. I don't think it started with you.
Let me look closer at what's holding this…
c: You turned the Fool. Face down, all three, and you took the only one in full sun.
Look at the sky behind him. Gold, and not one cloud in it.
You asked whether you'll find a new soulmate after your loss. The light is still on that day, and that's what I keep looking at.
But nobody has come. And you're the one carrying that question now.
Something turns up the moment this would go anywhere. I don't think any of it began with you.
Let me look closer at what's behind it…
